model.name: INTERP picert, seed 0, step 6,000
model.about: one attention head over the program's rows, then a readout over the program's names and the snap

prompt.note: REGS's counted input 0 for mul (stream eval, base 2026)

program.note: REGS's hand-written listing (REGS.md section 4). It stands in for the step where the model writes the program; no model wrote it.

run.note: every lookup of every instruction is one event of INTERP's frozen core (picert, seed 0, step 6,000), run on this machine

answer.note: read from the machine's memory at HALT

program.text:
0      row LDI  [J] -> BD
  1          JEQ  BD HASH end
  2          MOV  PA0 -> I
  3          MOV  KB -> K
  4          SET  0 -> CARRY
  5    inner LDI  [I] -> U
  6          JEQ  U HASH rowend
  7          LDI  [K] -> V
  8          MAC  U BD -> V
  9          STI  V -> [K]
 10          NBR  I NEXT -> I
 11          NBR  K NEXT -> K
 12          JMP  inner
 13   rowend MOV  CARRY -> V
 14          STI  V -> [K]
 15          NBR  J NEXT -> J
 16          NBR  KB NEXT -> KB
 17          JMP  row
 18      end HALT

certificate.covers: every program with at most 256 lines and 256 memory names in base 10, for any number of steps (REGS Theorem R1)

codebook.projection: the program's line codes, centred, on their top three principal directions; each instruction's point is the next-line lookup's output before the snap
